items.title: AI-powered conversational business problem discovery
items.description: The planner-service shall provide an AI-powered conversational interface that enables GoA staff to describe their business problems in plain language. The system shall use a large language model (Anthropic Claude) to progressively elicit and clarify the business problem without requiring users to have prior knowledge of ADSP services, architectural patterns, or technical terminology.
items.rationale: Current ADSP adoption is hampered by the requirement for users to understand service architecture before they can articulate their needs. Conversational AI removes this barrier by meeting users at their level of domain knowledge and guiding them through structured discovery.
items.acceptanceCriteria: A GoA business analyst with no ADSP knowledge can describe a business problem in conversational language and receive a structured business model summary after 3-5 exchanges without prompting for technical terms.

items.title: Structured business model construction from conversation
items.description: The system shall incrementally construct a structured business model from conversational input, classifying identified elements as Actors, Goals, Activities, Decisions, Business Rules, Workflows, Constraints, Outcomes, or other business concept types. The business model shall serve as the primary reasoning artifact for the Planning Agent, replacing reliance on raw conversation history.
items.rationale: Reasoning over a structured model rather than raw conversation history allows the Planning Agent to maintain coherent understanding across long sessions, survive compaction, and produce verifiable hypotheses grounded in identified business concepts rather than recency bias.
items.acceptanceCriteria: After a planning session, the business model JSON contains at least three classified business concepts with correct type assignments, demonstrating the agent's ability to infer structure from unstructured input.

items.title: Solution hypothesis generation in plain language
items.description: Once the planning agent has achieved sufficient confidence in the business model, it shall generate one or more ADSP-based solution hypotheses and present them to the user in plain, non-technical language. Each hypothesis shall identify the relevant ADSP services, explain the reasoning behind their selection, and propose a high-level implementation order.
items.rationale: Users should receive actionable recommendations presented accessibly without needing to translate technical recommendations. Plain-language presentation respects the range of technical literacy among GoA staff and supports decision-making by non-technical sponsors.
items.acceptanceCriteria: Generated hypotheses must include at least one named ADSP service, a plain-language summary, and a reasoning explanation. A user without ADSP knowledge should be able to read the summary and understand the proposed approach.

items.title: Persistent planning sessions resumable across sessions
items.description: Planning sessions shall persist across browser sessions and closures. A user shall be able to close the browser, return hours or days later, and resume the exact planning state including conversation history, business model state, open questions, specialist progress, and recommended next steps — without re-entering previously supplied information.
items.rationale: Complex GoA business problems often require multi-day planning engagements with input from multiple stakeholders. A session that loses state on browser close would be unusable for real-world planning work and would undermine user trust in the tool.
items.acceptanceCriteria: A user who closes the browser mid-session and returns the next day can resume the session with all prior context intact, as evidenced by the Planning Agent correctly referencing previously discussed concepts without re-prompting.

items.title: GoA business pattern recognition and accelerated planning
items.description: The planner-service shall maintain a configurable library of known GoA business process patterns (e.g., Case Management, Grant Application, Permit/Licence Application) and proactively identify when a user's business problem matches a known pattern. Pattern matches shall accelerate hypothesis generation and provide pre-defined clarifying questions specific to the matched pattern.
items.rationale: GoA operates a well-understood set of recurring business application types. Pattern recognition reduces the conversational overhead required to build a complete business model, accelerates time-to-hypothesis, and ensures proven ADSP service compositions are surfaced for common use cases.
items.acceptanceCriteria: When a user describes a business problem matching a configured pattern, the system identifies the pattern match within 3 exchanges and applies the pattern's clarifying questions and service mappings to the hypothesis.

items.title: Specialist agent coordination for deep service guidance
items.description: The planner-service shall coordinate a network of specialist sub-agents, each with deep knowledge of one ADSP service (form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, notification-service in MVP). The Planning Agent shall delegate service-specific questions to appropriate specialists and integrate their responses into the overall solution hypothesis. Specialists shall also be directly accessible by users for detailed implementation guidance.
items.rationale: The Planning Agent cannot maintain deep implementation knowledge across all ADSP services without becoming unwieldy. Delegation to specialists allows the Planning Agent to remain focused on problem understanding and solution coordination while enabling deep per-service expertise.
items.acceptanceCriteria: When a planning session involves form-service, the Planning Agent delegates form-specific questions to the form-service specialist and incorporates the response into the session state. The user can also directly invoke the form-service specialist workspace.

items.title: Multi-tenant data isolation following ADSP platform conventions
items.description: All planning data (sessions, business models, hypotheses, messages) shall be strictly isolated per ADSP tenant. The service shall follow ADSP platform multi-tenancy patterns and ensure no cross-tenant data access is possible at any layer (API, database, event bus). Session access shall be further scoped to the creating user within the tenant.
items.rationale: ADSP tenants are distinct GoA organizational units with separate data governance responsibilities. A cross-tenant data leak in the planner-service would be a material security incident. ADSP platform conventions provide well-tested patterns for achieving this isolation.
items.acceptanceCriteria: A user authenticated as Tenant A cannot retrieve, list, or modify sessions belonging to Tenant B, verified by API-level tests with cross-tenant token forgery attempts returning HTTP 403.

items.title: Full ADSP platform service pattern compliance
items.description: The planner-service shall be implemented as a first-class ADSP platform service, following all established ADSP service patterns: initializePlatform() SDK initialization, Keycloak JWT authentication via passport-jwt, MongoDB for all persistent data, RabbitMQ for domain events, Express 5 router patterns, domain event definitions, and configuration schema registration with the Configuration Service.
items.rationale: Platform convention compliance ensures that the planner-service can be operated, monitored, upgraded, and maintained by the ADSP Platform Team using the same tools and processes used for all other ADSP services. It also enables the service to benefit from platform-level capabilities such as tenant management and configuration versioning.
items.acceptanceCriteria: The planner-service passes the ADSP platform service compliance checklist: initializePlatform() is called at startup, all routes are Keycloak-JWT-protected, MongoDB schemas are defined, at least one domain event type is registered, and the service configuration schema is registered.

items.title: GoA Design System 2.0 compliant UI with accessibility
items.description: All user interface components for the planner-service (planning workspace, session list, specialist workspaces, pattern management) shall be implemented using GoA Design System 2.0 (@abgov/react-components) and integrated as new pages within the Tenant Management Webapp. All UI components shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility requirements.
items.rationale: GoA Design System compliance ensures a consistent user experience across all ADSP tools, builds user familiarity, and fulfills the GoA's accessibility obligations under provincial legislation. TMW integration avoids fragmenting the administrator's workflow across multiple applications.
items.acceptanceCriteria: All new UI pages use only @abgov/react-components components, pass automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks (axe-core), and are reachable via the existing TMW navigation structure for authenticated users.

items.title: Role-based access control with audit logging
items.description: The planner-service shall enforce role-based access control using Keycloak JWT roles (planner-user, planner-admin, tenant-admin). All administrative actions (pattern management, specialist configuration) shall require the appropriate role and shall be recorded in an immutable audit log. Access control decisions shall be enforced at the API layer.
items.rationale: Role-based access control ensures that pattern library management and specialist configuration are restricted to authorized administrators, preventing unauthorized modification of shared resources. Audit logging supports accountability and compliance with GoA governance requirements.
items.acceptanceCriteria: A user with only the planner-user role receives HTTP 403 when attempting to create or modify a business pattern. All administrative actions are recorded in the audit log with actor, action, timestamp, and affected resource.

items.title: Business analyst natural language problem description
items.description: A GoA business analyst with no ADSP knowledge shall be able to describe their business problem in natural, unstructured language. The system shall accept input in plain conversational English without requiring structured input, technical terminology, or prior system knowledge. The analyst shall receive progressive guidance through clarifying questions.
items.rationale: The primary value proposition of the planner-service is reducing the barrier to ADSP adoption. If the input interface requires structured format knowledge, the barrier is not removed. Natural language input with intelligent guidance is the core requirement for this stakeholder.
items.fitCriterion: A business analyst can complete a planning session and receive a solution hypothesis without typing any ADSP service names, technical terms, or structured data fields.

items.title: Business model visibility and correction
items.description: A GoA business analyst shall be able to view the structured business model that the Planning Agent has constructed from their conversation. The analyst shall be able to identify and correct misclassified concepts, missing relationships, or incorrect assumptions. Corrections shall be reflected in the model and used to update any derived hypotheses.
items.rationale: Transparency in the business model gives the analyst confidence that the AI understands their problem correctly. The ability to correct misinterpretations prevents the agent from generating hypotheses based on flawed premises, which would erode trust.
items.fitCriterion: The analyst can view the current business model in the UI and edit at least concept names and types. After correction, re-generating the hypothesis reflects the updated model.

items.title: Solution hypothesis in plain language with reasoning
items.description: A GoA business analyst shall receive solution hypotheses presented entirely in plain, non-technical language. Each hypothesis shall include a summary of the proposed solution, an explanation of why each recommended ADSP service was chosen, and the confidence basis. Technical ADSP implementation details shall be accessible on demand but not presented by default.
items.rationale: Business analysts are the primary decision-makers for solution direction but are not typically ADSP-technical. Plain-language presentation enables them to make informed decisions without depending on a developer translator. On-demand technical detail serves developers in the same workflow.
items.fitCriterion: An evaluator without ADSP knowledge can read the hypothesis summary and correctly describe what the proposed system will do and why, without consulting additional documentation.

items.title: Session persistence and cross-session resumption
items.description: A GoA business analyst or developer shall be able to close the browser or end their work session at any point and resume later with full context restoration. The session shall restore all prior conversation context, the current business model, open questions, specialist-agent outputs, and recommended next steps. The user shall not need to re-describe any previously provided information.
items.rationale: Planning work is not always completed in one sitting. Session persistence that survives browser close and supports multi-day work is essential for the tool to be usable in real GoA project workflows.
items.fitCriterion: A user who closes the browser with an active session and returns 24 hours later is presented with their session in the correct state, and the Planning Agent acknowledges prior context without re-prompting.

items.title: GoA developer feeds existing requirements or code
items.description: A GoA developer shall be able to provide existing requirements documentation or application code as input to the planner. The Planning Agent shall analyze this input to identify gaps, ambiguities, and potential ADSP service integration points, without requiring the developer to re-describe the problem from scratch.
items.rationale: Many GoA projects have partial documentation or existing applications that need enhancement. Allowing structured input beyond natural conversation accelerates the planning process for technical users and ensures ADSP services are considered for enhancement of existing systems.
items.fitCriterion: A developer can paste requirements text or describe an existing application, and the Planning Agent identifies at least two gap or ADSP integration opportunities without additional prompting.

items.title: Specialist agent deep technical guidance
items.description: A GoA developer shall be able to consult specialist agents for deep, service-specific implementation guidance on form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, and notification-service. The specialist shall answer configuration questions, validate proposed designs, and provide implementation recommendations at the level of detail needed to begin implementation.
items.rationale: The Planning Agent alone cannot provide the depth of service-specific knowledge needed for implementation. Specialist agents bridge the gap between high-level solution hypothesis and actionable implementation guidance.
items.fitCriterion: A developer consulting the form-service specialist receives specific guidance on form schema, workflow configuration, and integration patterns relevant to their identified business problem.

items.title: Tenant administrator manages business pattern library
items.description: An ADSP tenant administrator shall be able to create, update, deactivate, and view business pattern templates through the TMW administrative interface. Pattern management shall require the planner-admin or tenant-admin role. Changes shall take effect immediately for pattern matching in subsequent sessions.
items.rationale: Different GoA departments have unique business processes that may not be covered by the global pattern library. Tenant-specific patterns allow departments to capture their own process knowledge and accelerate planning for recurring problem types within their organization.
items.fitCriterion: An administrator creates a new business pattern, starts a new session describing a problem matching that pattern, and the agent identifies the pattern match and applies its clarifying questions.

items.title: Multi-tenant data isolation
items.description: The ADSP Platform Team shall be able to verify that planning sessions, business models, hypotheses, and messages from one tenant are never accessible to users authenticated as a different tenant. Data isolation shall apply at all system layers: REST API, MongoDB, and RabbitMQ events.
items.rationale: Multi-tenant isolation is a foundational requirement for ADSP platform services. Any cross-tenant data leak in the planner-service would constitute a security incident and breach of trust with GoA departments.
items.fitCriterion: Cross-tenant access attempts via authenticated API requests return HTTP 403. MongoDB queries are scoped with tenant filters. RabbitMQ events include tenantId and are consumed only by the emitting tenant.

items.title: ADSP platform SDK and service pattern compliance
items.description: The ADSP Platform Team shall be able to verify that the planner-service follows all mandated ADSP platform service patterns: initializePlatform() initialization, Keycloak JWT authentication, MongoDB schemas, RabbitMQ domain event definitions, Express 5 router patterns, and Configuration Service schema registration.
items.rationale: Platform-convention compliance allows the ADSP Platform Team to operate, upgrade, and troubleshoot the planner-service using their existing tooling and processes, without special-casing the service.
items.fitCriterion: The service startup log shows initializePlatform() completion. Keycloak JWT validation protects all endpoints. MongoDB collections are schema-validated. Domain events are registered and emitted on lifecycle transitions.

items.title: Accessible GoA Design System 2.0 UI in TMW
items.description: All UI components shall use GoA Design System 2.0 (@abgov/react-components) exclusively and shall be integrated into TMW as new navigable pages accessible from the TMW sidebar. Components shall meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA and support keyboard-only navigation and screen readers.
items.rationale: GoA accessibility legislation and Design System adoption policy require all new government digital interfaces to meet these standards. Using @abgov/react-components exclusively ensures consistency and leverages pre-built accessible components.
items.fitCriterion: Automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks (axe-core) pass on all new pages. All interactive elements are keyboard-navigable. All pages render correctly using the GoA Design System component library.

items.title: Role-based access control enforcement
items.description: The planner-service shall enforce role-based access control using Keycloak JWT roles for all API endpoints. The planner-user role shall have access to session management and agent interaction. The planner-admin role shall additionally have access to pattern management. The tenant-admin role shall have full administrative access. All access control decisions shall be enforced server-side.
items.rationale: Server-side RBAC prevents privilege escalation via client-side manipulation. Separating user and admin roles limits the blast radius of a compromised user account and protects the shared pattern library from unauthorized modification.
items.fitCriterion: API integration tests confirm that all protected endpoints return HTTP 403 for requests with insufficient roles and HTTP 200 for requests with the correct roles.

items.title: Audit logging for all administrative and security-relevant actions
items.description: All administrative actions (pattern CRUD, specialist configuration changes) and security-relevant events (authentication failures, authorization denials, data access) shall be recorded in an immutable audit log. Audit records shall include actor identity, action, timestamp, affected resource, and tenant context.
items.rationale: Audit logging is required for GoA governance compliance and supports incident investigation. Immutability prevents retroactive concealment of unauthorized actions and supports non-repudiation.
items.fitCriterion: After a pattern management action, the audit log contains an entry with the correct actor, action type, timestamp, and pattern ID. The log cannot be modified by application operators.

items.title: Session export for stakeholder sharing
items.description: A GoA business analyst or developer shall be able to export the current state of a planning session as a structured JSON document. The export shall include the business model, solution hypotheses, open questions, and recommended next steps in a portable, non-proprietary format usable for stakeholder review.
items.rationale: Planning outputs need to be shared with stakeholders who may not have TMW access. A structured JSON export enables downstream processing, stakeholder review, and record-keeping without requiring access to the live system.
items.fitCriterion: The exported JSON file contains business model concepts, at least one solution hypothesis, and session metadata. The file is valid JSON importable by standard tooling.

items.title: LLM response performance within acceptable bounds
items.description: Under normal load conditions (up to 5 concurrent users per tenant, 50 LLM requests per hour per tenant), the system shall return AI agent responses within 30 seconds at the 95th percentile. The UI shall provide feedback to the user during AI processing to prevent the appearance of system unresponsiveness.
items.rationale: LLM inference is inherently slower than database reads. Without performance requirements and user feedback, users may interpret normal processing delay as a system failure, degrading the user experience and trust in the tool.
items.fitCriterion: Under the specified load profile, 95th percentile response time is within 30 seconds. The UI displays a progress indicator during AI processing.

items.title: Conversational AI planning interface via Anthropic Claude
items.description: The system shall expose a conversational REST API endpoint enabling multi-turn dialogue between users and the Planning Agent powered by Anthropic Claude. Each request shall include the current conversation history, business model context, and a system prompt encoding the agent persona and reasoning instructions. The response shall include the agent reply and any updated business model state.
items.rationale: The conversational API is the core interaction mechanism of the planner-service. Using Anthropic Claude as the LLM backend provides the reasoning capability necessary for business problem elicitation and model construction. Structured context injection ensures coherent multi-turn reasoning.
items.fitCriterion: POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages returns a valid agent response incorporating prior conversation context within 30 seconds for a well-formed request.

items.title: Incremental business model construction engine
items.description: The system shall maintain and update a structured BusinessModel document for each planning session. After each Planning Agent turn, the system shall parse the agent output to identify newly mentioned business concepts and their types, update the model document atomically in MongoDB, and increment the model version counter. The model shall be used as the primary context for subsequent agent turns.
items.rationale: Grounding the agent reasoning in a structured model rather than raw conversation history ensures robustness to context window truncation and provides a verifiable audit trail of the agent understanding evolution over the session lifetime.
items.fitCriterion: After five conversational turns, the BusinessModel document contains classified concepts drawn from the conversation, with correct conceptType assignments for at least 80% of explicitly mentioned entities.

items.title: Business pattern matching against configured pattern library
items.description: The system shall evaluate the current business model against all active BusinessPattern records for the tenant after each model update. Pattern matching shall consider domain language overlap, concept type distribution, and strong signal presence. When the matching confidence for a pattern exceeds the configured threshold (default 60 out of 100), the system shall surface the pattern match to the Planning Agent and provide the pattern clarifying questions.
items.rationale: Pattern matching accelerates the planning process by recognising recurring GoA business process types and providing pre-validated ADSP service compositions. This reduces both the number of clarifying exchanges needed and the risk of recommending non-standard service combinations.
items.fitCriterion: A session describing a case management process triggers the Case Management pattern match within five exchanges and applies pattern-defined clarifying questions in the subsequent agent turn.

items.title: Solution hypothesis generation and versioned management
items.description: When the BusinessModel confidenceScore reaches or exceeds 70, the system shall trigger hypothesis generation via the Planning Agent. The agent shall produce a SolutionHypothesis document containing the recommended ADSP services, plain-language summary, reasoning explanation, and proposed implementation order. Hypotheses shall be versioned and their status lifecycle managed through the states: draft, proposed, accepted, rejected, and superseded.
items.rationale: Formal hypothesis records provide a persistent, reviewable output from the planning engagement. Version tracking supports iterative refinement and prevents loss of previous hypotheses when new ones supersede them.
items.fitCriterion: When confidenceScore reaches 70, a SolutionHypothesis is created in MongoDB with status 'proposed', at least one ADSP service in adspServices, and a non-empty summary and reasoning field.

items.title: Persistent session storage with full state restoration
items.description: The system shall persist all planning session state to MongoDB, including conversation messages (append-only), the current BusinessModel version, all SolutionHypothesis records, open questions list, specialist progress map, and next steps list. On session resume, the system shall reconstruct the complete agent context from persisted state, enabling the Planning Agent to reference prior conversation content without re-prompting the user.
items.rationale: Full state persistence is the technical enabler for multi-day planning engagements. The MongoDB data model must capture all state that the Planning Agent needs to reason coherently across sessions, including its own prior reasoning artifacts.
items.fitCriterion: A session paused after five turns and resumed 24 hours later produces an agent response that correctly references at least one concept from the prior session without user re-prompting.

items.title: Business pattern CRUD via ADSP Configuration Service
items.description: The system shall store and retrieve BusinessPattern records via the ADSP Configuration Service. Pattern management operations (create, read, update, deactivate) shall be exposed via REST API endpoints protected by the planner-admin role. The system shall cache pattern data locally with a 5-minute TTL to reduce Configuration Service call frequency.
items.rationale: Storing patterns in the Configuration Service enables tenants to leverage the platform existing configuration versioning capabilities without building a redundant configuration store. Pattern caching reduces Configuration Service call volume.
items.fitCriterion: GET /api/v1/patterns returns active patterns. POST /api/v1/patterns creates a pattern accessible in subsequent sessions. PUT /api/v1/patterns/{id}/deactivate removes the pattern from matching.

items.title: Specialist agent orchestration and delegation protocol
items.description: The system shall implement an agent orchestration protocol enabling the Planning Agent to delegate specific questions to specialist agents for form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, and notification-service. Delegation requests shall include the relevant session context and the specific question. Specialist responses shall be returned to the Planning Agent for integration into session state. Users shall be able to navigate directly to specialist workspaces from the planning session.
items.rationale: The orchestration protocol is the core mechanism for maintaining separation of concerns between the Planning Agent broad coordination role and each specialist deep service knowledge. Clear delegation protocols enable each agent to focus on its domain.
items.fitCriterion: When the Planning Agent identifies a form-service question, a delegation request is logged in the session specialistProgress map, the form specialist API is invoked with correct context, and the response is integrated into the session state.

items.title: Anthropic Claude API integration with resilient error handling
items.description: The system shall integrate with the Anthropic Claude API via the @anthropic-ai/sdk package. API calls shall include retry logic with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) for transient failures. Rate limit responses shall surface a user-visible message and pause the session. The Anthropic API key shall be stored in a platform-managed secrets store, never in source code or configuration files.
items.rationale: Robust error handling for external LLM API calls prevents transient network failures from disrupting active planning sessions. Secret management follows ADSP platform security requirements.
items.fitCriterion: A simulated Anthropic API timeout results in automatic retry and eventual success or a clear user-facing error message. API key is read from environment variable at runtime, not hardcoded.

items.title: Keycloak JWT authentication via ADSP platform SDK
items.description: All planner-service REST API endpoints shall require a valid Keycloak JWT bearer token, validated using the passport-jwt strategy as configured by the ADSP platform SDK. Token validation shall verify the issuer, audience, expiry, and signature. Requests with invalid, expired, or missing tokens shall receive HTTP 401. The JWT shall carry the tenantId and userId claims used for data scoping.
items.rationale: Keycloak JWT authentication is the mandated ADSP platform authentication mechanism. Delegating token validation to the platform SDK ensures consistent behaviour with all other ADSP services and reduces the risk of custom authentication implementation defects.
items.fitCriterion: A request with no Authorization header returns HTTP 401. A request with an expired token returns HTTP 401. A request with a valid token proceeds to authorization checks.

items.title: MongoDB persistence with tenant-scoped data isolation
items.description: The system shall use MongoDB via Mongoose for all persistent data storage. All MongoDB documents shall include a tenantId field, and all queries shall include a tenantId filter matching the authenticated user tenant. MongoDB collection schemas shall be defined with field-level validation. Indexes shall be defined on tenantId, userId, and sessionId fields for query performance.
items.rationale: MongoDB is the ADSP platform mandated persistence layer. Tenant-scoped filtering at the database query level provides defence-in-depth against cross-tenant data leakage beyond API-layer access control checks.
items.fitCriterion: Every MongoDB collection has tenantId as an indexed field. All read queries include a tenantId filter. Attempting to retrieve a document for a different tenantId via database inspection returns no result.

items.title: RabbitMQ domain event publication for session lifecycle
items.description: The system shall publish domain events to the ADSP platform RabbitMQ message broker for all significant planning session lifecycle events: session-created, session-updated, session-completed, session-archived, hypothesis-generated, and specialist-delegated. Each event shall include the tenantId, sessionId, eventType, and a structured payload. Event definitions shall be registered with the ADSP event service during initializePlatform().
items.rationale: Domain event publication is a core ADSP platform service pattern that enables other platform components to react to planner-service lifecycle events and supports platform-level audit and monitoring.
items.fitCriterion: Creating a session publishes a session-created event to RabbitMQ with correct tenantId and sessionId. The event is consumed by the platform event log without errors.

items.title: ADSP initializePlatform() SDK startup registration
items.description: The system shall call the ADSP SDK initializePlatform() function during service startup, registering the service configuration schema, domain event definitions, health check endpoints, and service metadata with the ADSP platform. The service shall not begin serving API requests until initializePlatform() completes successfully.
items.rationale: The initializePlatform() call is the ADSP platform mandated startup protocol that registers the service with platform-wide management infrastructure. Failing to call it leaves the service invisible to platform monitoring and configuration tools.
items.fitCriterion: The service startup log records successful initializePlatform() completion before the Express server begins accepting connections. Health check endpoint returns 200 after initialization.

items.title: Three-level RBAC with role hierarchy enforcement
items.description: The system shall enforce role-based access control using three roles from the Keycloak JWT: planner-user (session management and agent interaction), planner-admin (all planner-user permissions plus pattern management), and tenant-admin (all planner-admin permissions plus user role assignment). Role checks shall be enforced at the route handler level. Insufficient role shall return HTTP 403.
items.rationale: A three-level role hierarchy provides granular access control that limits the blast radius of compromised user accounts and ensures sensitive administrative operations are restricted to authorized staff.
items.fitCriterion: API tests confirm planner-user cannot access pattern management endpoints (returns 403). planner-admin can access all pattern endpoints. tenant-admin can access all endpoints.

items.title: WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessible GoA Design System UI
items.description: All UI components in the planner-service TMW integration shall conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Requirements include keyboard-only navigation for all interactive elements, sufficient colour contrast ratios, semantic HTML with ARIA labels on interactive controls, visible focus indicators, text alternatives for non-text content, and correct heading hierarchy. Accessibility shall be verified by automated axe-core checks as part of the test suite.
items.rationale: WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance is a GoA accessibility policy requirement for all government digital interfaces. Using GoA Design System 2.0 components provides a strong baseline but custom compositions require explicit accessibility verification.
items.fitCriterion: All new TMW pages pass automated axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA scans with zero critical or serious violations. All interactive elements are operable via keyboard tab navigation.

items.title: LLM response performance — 30-second P95 under defined load profile
items.description: Under the defined load profile — up to 5 concurrent active users per tenant making LLM inference requests, up to 50 LLM requests per hour per tenant — the system shall return AI agent responses with end-to-end latency at or below 30 seconds at the 95th percentile. This load profile reflects the expected adoption curve in the first 12 months of deployment. Streaming responses shall begin delivering content within 5 seconds of the Anthropic API first-token receipt.
items.rationale: LLM inference latency is outside the service direct control but must be bounded to maintain a usable planning experience. The 30-second P95 threshold accommodates Anthropic API processing time. Streaming prevents users from interpreting valid processing as a system hang.
items.fitCriterion: Performance test with 5 concurrent users generating 50 requests/hour shows P95 response time at or below 30 seconds. First token appears in the UI within 5 seconds for streaming responses.

items.title: Session export as portable JSON document
items.description: The system shall provide a REST API endpoint (GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/export) that returns the complete planning session state as a single JSON document. The export shall include session metadata, business model (concepts and relationships), all solution hypotheses, open questions, and recommended next steps. The export shall be valid against the planner-service data_io_schema definitions.
items.rationale: Session export enables users to share planning outputs with stakeholders without TMW access. A structured JSON format supports downstream processing and preserves all planning artifacts in a non-proprietary format.
items.fitCriterion: GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/export returns a valid JSON document containing businessModel, hypotheses, and sessionMetadata. The response validates against the data_io_schema.

items.title: Resilient LLM API calls with retry and circuit breaker
items.description: The system shall wrap all Anthropic Claude API calls with transient fault handling: exponential backoff retry (3 retries, base delay 1 second, max delay 16 seconds) for 5xx responses and connection timeouts; circuit breaker that opens after 3 consecutive failures within 30 seconds and closes after 60 seconds; graceful degradation surfacing a clear user message when the circuit is open.
items.rationale: The Anthropic Claude API is an external dependency outside the service direct control. Retry logic handles transient API issues. A circuit breaker prevents cascading failures when the API is degraded for extended periods.
items.fitCriterion: Simulated Anthropic API 503 responses trigger automatic retry with correct backoff. After 3 consecutive failures, subsequent requests receive a clear user-facing error without additional API calls.

items.title: OWASP ASVS Level 2 security conformance
items.description: The planner-service shall conform to the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard Level 2, appropriate for a Protected B information system. Applicable controls shall include: parameterised database queries, output encoding in all API responses, rate limiting on authentication and sensitive endpoints, input validation with maximum lengths and type enforcement, dependency vulnerability scanning in the build pipeline, and TLS 1.2 or higher for all communications.
items.rationale: GoA planning session data may contain sensitive organizational information at Protected B classification. ASVS Level 2 provides a proven security baseline for this classification level.
items.fitCriterion: OWASP ZAP passive scan passes without High severity findings. All database queries use parameterised form. Dependency scan shows no Critical CVEs in direct dependencies.

items.title: TLS 1.2 enforcement and HTTPS-only access
items.description: All communications to and from the planner-service shall use TLS 1.2 or higher. HTTP requests shall be redirected to HTTPS. HSTS headers shall be set on all responses. Cookies shall be marked Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Strict. Service-to-service calls to external APIs and ADSP services shall use TLS. Response bodies and logs shall not contain sensitive data in cleartext.
items.rationale: TLS enforcement protects planning session content from interception during transit. HSTS and cookie security attributes prevent protocol downgrade and cross-site attacks.
items.fitCriterion: HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS with 301. All API responses include Strict-Transport-Security header. No plaintext service-to-service calls exist (verified by inspection).

items.title: Administrative audit logging with HMAC tamper-evidence
items.description: The system shall maintain an audit log for all administrative actions and security-relevant events. Each audit record shall include: timestamp, actor identity (userId and tenantId), action type, affected resource identifier, and outcome. The audit log shall be append-only and shall implement an HMAC integrity chain to detect unauthorized modification of audit entries.
items.rationale: Audit logging is required for GoA governance and regulatory compliance. Tamper-evidence via HMAC chaining prevents retroactive modification of audit records and supports non-repudiation.
items.fitCriterion: After a pattern creation, the audit log contains an entry with correct actor, action, and patternId. Modifying an audit record changes the HMAC chain, causing subsequent record verification to fail.

items.title: Session inactivity timeout with per-role configuration
items.description: The system shall enforce session inactivity timeouts: 60 minutes for planner-user, 30 minutes for planner-admin. Timeout durations shall be configurable per role via the ADSP Configuration Service. On timeout, the user token shall be invalidated and the user prompted to re-authenticate. In-progress conversation state shall be preserved for session resumption after re-authentication.
items.rationale: Inactivity timeout limits the exposure window for unattended authenticated sessions on shared government workstations. Per-role configurability allows stricter timeouts for administrative roles.
items.fitCriterion: After the configured inactivity period, subsequent requests return HTTP 401 and the UI prompts re-authentication. After re-authentication, the session state is restored without data loss.

items.title: Data retention and disposition policy per GoA regulations
items.description: The system shall implement a configurable data retention policy for planning session data. The default retention period shall be 2 years from session completion or archiving. After the period elapses, sessions and associated data shall be subject to automated archiving or destruction per the GoA Information Management Regulation. The retention period shall be configurable per tenant.
items.rationale: GoA Information Management Regulation requires defined retention and disposition procedures for all government records. Planning sessions may contain business analysis data constituting GoA records.
items.fitCriterion: Sessions with updatedAt beyond the configured retention period are flagged for disposition in the next scheduled run. A tenant can configure a custom retention period via the Configuration Service.

items.title: Service health monitoring and structured observability
items.description: The system shall expose health check endpoints (/health/live and /health/ready) returning service status and dependency health. The service shall integrate with ADSP platform monitoring by publishing structured JSON log entries and metrics. Alerts shall be configurable for LLM API failures, high error rates, and session processing failures.
items.rationale: Operational observability is required for the ADSP Platform Team to maintain the service SLA and detect degradation before it impacts users. Structured logging enables log aggregation and automated alerting.
items.fitCriterion: GET /health/live returns 200 with JSON service status. When MongoDB is unavailable, /health/ready returns 503. Log entries are valid JSON with standard fields.

items.title: Server-side input validation with field-level error responses
items.description: The system shall validate all API request inputs server-side before processing. Validation shall enforce field type conformance, maximum string lengths (conversation content: 10000 characters, session title: 200 characters, pattern fields: 5000 characters), required field presence, and enum value conformance. Validation failures shall return HTTP 400 with field-level error details. Client-side validation is supplementary only.
items.rationale: Server-side input validation is the last reliable barrier against injection attacks and invalid state in the database. Client-side validation alone is insufficient as it can be bypassed.
items.fitCriterion: A request with conversation content exceeding 10000 characters returns HTTP 400 with a field-level error. A request omitting a required field returns HTTP 400 with the missing field identified.

items.title: Anthropic SDK integration with conversation context management
items.description: The software shall integrate with the Anthropic Claude API using the @anthropic-ai/sdk npm package. The API client shall be initialized with the API key from environment variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at startup. Conversation context shall be assembled as an array of message objects from the session ConversationMessage history, prepended with a system prompt. Messages shall be truncated to fit within the model context window using a sliding window strategy.
items.rationale: Using the official Anthropic SDK ensures compatibility with API versioning and provides typed interfaces. Context window management is critical for long-running sessions to prevent exceeding token limits.
items.fitCriterion: The service successfully calls the Anthropic API with a correctly assembled context array. When message history exceeds 80% of the context window, older messages are truncated while preserving the business model summary.

items.title: Planning session REST API controller
items.description: The software shall implement an Express 5 router providing REST endpoints for session management: POST /api/v1/sessions (create), GET /api/v1/sessions (list paginated), GET /api/v1/sessions/{id} (retrieve), PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id} (update status), DELETE /api/v1/sessions/{id} (archive), POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages (send message), GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/export (export). All endpoints shall be protected by Keycloak JWT middleware scoped to the authenticated user tenant.
items.rationale: A clear RESTful API contract with consistent endpoint conventions follows ADSP platform standards and enables the TMW frontend to integrate predictably. Separate message endpoint supports streaming responses independently of session CRUD.
items.fitCriterion: All seven endpoint paths exist, return correct HTTP status codes, and include OpenAPI annotations matching the data_io_schema definitions.

items.title: BusinessModel Mongoose schema and tenant-scoped repository
items.description: The software shall define a Mongoose schema for the BusinessModel entity with all fields from data_io_schema.json $defs/BusinessModel, including embedded BusinessConcept sub-documents. The schema shall enforce field types, required fields, and enum constraints. A repository layer shall abstract all MongoDB operations for BusinessModel, enforcing tenantId scoping on all queries.
items.rationale: Schema-level validation provides defence-in-depth data integrity beyond API-level validation. Repository pattern abstraction enables unit testing with mock implementations and isolates database logic.
items.fitCriterion: Attempting to save a BusinessModel document without a required field throws a Mongoose validation error. All repository methods include tenantId as a mandatory query filter.

items.title: Pattern matching service with composite confidence scoring
items.description: The software shall implement a PatternMatchingService class that scores the current BusinessModel against each active BusinessPattern. The scoring algorithm shall compute domain language overlap ratio, strong signal presence count, and concept type distribution match. The composite score shall be normalised to 0-100. Scores at or above the configured threshold (default 60) shall be returned as candidate matches sorted by score descending.
items.rationale: A deterministic explainable scoring algorithm allows the Planning Agent to surface pattern matches with quantified confidence and present the reasoning transparently to users.
items.fitCriterion: Unit tests confirm a BusinessModel with Case Management strong signals scores at or above 60 against the Case Management pattern. A model with no matching concepts scores below 20.

items.title: SolutionHypothesis generation service triggered by confidence threshold
items.description: The software shall implement a HypothesisGenerationService triggered when the BusinessModel confidenceScore reaches or exceeds 70. The service shall assemble a structured hypothesis generation prompt incorporating the business model state and matched pattern if any, call the Anthropic Claude API, parse the response into a SolutionHypothesis document, persist it to MongoDB, and update the session hypothesisIds array.
items.rationale: Separating hypothesis generation into a dedicated service enables independent testing, clear triggering semantics, and the ability to regenerate hypotheses when the business model changes.
items.fitCriterion: When confidenceScore is set to 70 or above, HypothesisGenerationService produces a SolutionHypothesis document with all required fields persisted to MongoDB with status 'proposed'.

items.title: Pattern management REST API with admin role guard
items.description: The software shall implement REST endpoints for business pattern management: POST /api/v1/patterns (create), GET /api/v1/patterns (list active), GET /api/v1/patterns/{id} (retrieve), PUT /api/v1/patterns/{id} (update), PUT /api/v1/patterns/{id}/deactivate (soft delete). All write endpoints shall require the planner-admin or tenant-admin role. The read endpoint shall be accessible to planner-user. Patterns shall be stored and retrieved via the ADSP Configuration Service integration.
items.rationale: Pattern management endpoints are a distinct capability set from session management requiring stricter access control. Separate router with explicit role guards follows the principle of least privilege.
items.fitCriterion: A planner-user role token returns HTTP 403 on POST /api/v1/patterns. A planner-admin role token returns HTTP 201 with valid payload. Deactivated patterns do not appear in GET /api/v1/patterns list.

items.title: Specialist agent invocation protocol with 60-second timeout
items.description: The software shall implement a SpecialistAgentService that routes delegation requests to specialist agent endpoints with a context payload including relevant session state excerpt and the specific question. Each specialist invocation shall enforce a timeout of 60 seconds. Specialist responses shall be stored in the session specialistProgress map and returned to the Planning Agent as structured context.
items.rationale: A dedicated specialist invocation service decouples the Planning Agent from knowledge of individual specialist endpoints. Timeout enforcement prevents a slow specialist from blocking the planning session.
items.fitCriterion: A delegation request to the form specialist completes within 60 seconds. A simulated specialist timeout is handled gracefully with the session continuing without the specialist response.

items.title: Tenant extraction middleware for request scoping
items.description: The software shall implement Express middleware that extracts the tenantId claim from the validated Keycloak JWT and attaches it to all request objects. All repository and service layer operations shall require tenantId as a parameter and shall fail if it is absent. The middleware shall validate that tenantId is a non-empty string before proceeding to route handlers.
items.rationale: Centralising tenant extraction in middleware provides a single enforcement point that is difficult to accidentally bypass. Requiring tenantId as an explicit parameter in the data layer makes cross-tenant operations visible.
items.fitCriterion: A request missing the tenantId claim after JWT validation returns HTTP 401. A request with tenantId set correctly reaches the route handler with req.tenantId populated.

items.title: Domain event publication service wrapping RabbitMQ
items.description: The software shall implement an EventPublicationService that wraps RabbitMQ publishing with event type validation, structured JSON payload serialization, tenantId inclusion, and delivery confirmation. The service shall register all domain event types with the ADSP event service during initializePlatform(). Failed event publications shall be logged with sessionId and event type but shall not fail the originating operation.
items.rationale: Wrapping RabbitMQ in a service layer enables event type validation and provides a single point for observability instrumentation. Non-blocking failure semantics prevents message queue issues from disrupting core planning workflows.
items.fitCriterion: Creating a session results in a session-created event in the RabbitMQ queue with correct structure. A simulated RabbitMQ failure is logged but does not cause the session creation to fail.

items.title: React planner workspace UI components using GoA Design System 2.0
items.description: The software shall implement React 18 components for the planner workspace using @abgov/react-components exclusively. Required components include: PlannerSessionList (paginated session list with status badges), PlannerChatInterface (streaming message display with typing indicator), BusinessModelViewer (structured concept list with type icons), HypothesisPanel (solution hypothesis display with reasoning toggle), and SpecialistNavigator (specialist workspace switcher).
items.rationale: Using exclusively GoA Design System components ensures compliance with the GoA Design System mandate and leverages pre-built accessible WCAG-compliant components. Custom components where DS alternatives exist is a compliance violation.
items.fitCriterion: All five component types use only @abgov/react-components (verified by dependency audit). Automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks pass on all rendered component trees.

items.title: Streaming LLM response delivery via server-sent events
items.description: The software shall implement server-sent events streaming for LLM responses from the POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/messages endpoint. The React frontend shall consume the SSE stream and progressively render the agent response text as it arrives. The first token shall appear in the UI within 5 seconds of the Anthropic API first-token receipt. A typing indicator shall display while the stream is open.
items.rationale: Streaming delivery dramatically improves perceived responsiveness for LLM-powered interfaces. Users see immediate progress rather than a blank wait period, which is the expected behaviour for modern AI chat interfaces.
items.fitCriterion: The message endpoint returns Content-Type: text/event-stream. The React frontend renders the first token within 5 seconds. Typing indicator appears during streaming and disappears on stream close.

items.title: ADSP Configuration Service adapter with in-memory cache
items.description: The software shall implement a ConfigurationServiceAdapter calling the ADSP Configuration Service REST API to store and retrieve BusinessPattern records for the authenticated tenant. The adapter shall implement a local in-memory cache with a 5-minute TTL for read operations. Cache invalidation shall occur immediately on pattern write operations. A fail-open fallback shall return cached data during Configuration Service unavailability.
items.rationale: Caching reduces Configuration Service call volume and protects pattern matching performance. Fail-open semantics ensures pattern matching continues during brief Configuration Service unavailability.
items.fitCriterion: Pattern read operations hit the cache after first fetch. A simulated Configuration Service outage does not prevent pattern matching using cached data. Cache is invalidated immediately after a pattern write.

items.title: Audit logging middleware with HMAC integrity chaining
items.description: The software shall implement audit logging middleware intercepting all administrative route handlers and recording structured audit events to a dedicated MongoDB audit_events collection. Each document shall include: eventId, timestamp, actorId, tenantId, action, resourceId, resourceType, outcome, and hmac (HMAC-SHA256 using AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY from environment). The hmac field of each event shall reference the previous event eventId for chain integrity.
items.rationale: Audit integrity chaining means modification of any audit record breaks the HMAC chain of all subsequent records, making tampering detectable. A dedicated collection separates audit data from operational data with different retention policies.
items.fitCriterion: After three administrative actions, the audit_events collection contains three chained documents. Modifying the second document action field fails HMAC verification for the third document.

items.title: Input validation middleware with schema-driven field-level errors
items.description: The software shall implement Express validation middleware using Joi or Zod for all API request bodies and query parameters. Validation rules shall be derived from data_io_schema.json constraints. Validation failures shall return HTTP 400 with a JSON body containing a field-level errors array of {field, message} objects. The middleware shall apply to all write endpoints.
items.rationale: Centralised validation middleware ensures consistent error response shapes. Schema-driven validation derived from data_io_schema reduces drift between data definition and validation rules.
items.fitCriterion: A POST /api/v1/sessions with an oversized title field returns HTTP 400 with errors array identifying the title field. An invalid status enum value returns HTTP 400.

items.title: LLMCallWrapper with retry and circuit breaker
items.description: The software shall implement a LLMCallWrapper class wrapping all Anthropic Claude API invocations with exponential backoff retry (max 3 retries, base 1000ms, max 16000ms) for HTTP 5xx and network timeout errors. A circuit breaker shall open after 3 consecutive failures within 30 seconds and close after 60 seconds. When the circuit is open, the wrapper throws CircuitOpenError surfaced as HTTP 503 with a user-visible message.
items.rationale: Retry logic handles transient Anthropic API failures. The circuit breaker prevents resource starvation when the API is genuinely unavailable. A dedicated wrapper class enables unit testing with injected failures.
items.fitCriterion: Unit tests confirm retry occurs with correct delays. After 3 failures the circuit opens and throws CircuitOpenError without additional API calls. Circuit closes after configured recovery time.

items.title: Health check endpoints and structured JSON logging
items.description: The software shall implement health check endpoints: GET /health/live (liveness) returns 200 if the process is running; GET /health/ready (readiness) returns 200 if MongoDB, RabbitMQ, and Anthropic API connectivity are confirmed (503 otherwise, with 5-second timeout per dependency). Both return ADSP-format JSON bodies. The service shall emit structured JSON log entries via Winston for all request and error events.
items.rationale: Health endpoints enable Kubernetes probes to manage service pod lifecycle correctly. Readiness checks prevent traffic routing to pods before dependencies are available. Structured logging enables centralised log aggregation.
items.fitCriterion: GET /health/live returns 200 immediately. GET /health/ready returns 503 when MongoDB is unreachable. All log entries are valid JSON with timestamp, level, message, and tenantId fields.

items.title: Accessible chat interface for natural language problem description
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need an accessible conversational interface where I can type or paste my business problem description in plain language and receive AI-guided questions and responses. The interface shall support full keyboard navigation, display clear focus states, and work correctly with screen readers. Conversation history shall scroll correctly and new messages shall be announced to screen readers.
items.rationale: Keyboard navigation and screen reader support ensure the interface is usable by all GoA staff regardless of ability, fulfilling the GoA accessibility mandate. Natural language input removes the barrier of requiring users to know ADSP terminology before engaging.

items.title: Session list with status indicators and resumption controls
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need to view a paginated list of my planning sessions with clear status indicators (active, paused, completed, archived) and a prominent Resume button for continuable sessions. The list shall be navigable by keyboard, filterable by status, and display session title, last activity date, and matched pattern if any. Resuming shall restore full conversation context within 3 seconds.
items.rationale: Users engaging in multi-day planning need a clear overview of all their sessions with quick-access resumption. Status indicators prevent confusion about which sessions are continuable versus completed, and keyboard accessibility ensures compliance with GoA accessibility obligations.

items.title: Business model viewer with editable concept classification
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need to view the structured business model the Planning Agent has built from my conversation, presented as a readable list of classified concepts with their types. I need to be able to correct the type of any misclassified concept without losing surrounding conversation context. Changes shall take effect immediately in the model view.
items.rationale: Transparency in the AI-constructed model builds user trust and allows correction of misinterpretations before they propagate into hypotheses. Direct inline editing reduces the friction of correction, making it practical for users to maintain model accuracy throughout a session.

items.title: Hypothesis panel with plain-language summary and expandable reasoning
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need to view solution hypotheses in a clearly structured panel presenting the plain-language summary prominently, with ADSP service names, reasoning, and implementation order accessible via expandable sections. The hypothesis status shall be visually clear. I shall be able to mark a hypothesis as accepted or request a revised hypothesis.
items.rationale: Business analysts are the primary decision-makers for solution direction but are not typically ADSP-technical. A panel that leads with plain language and makes technical detail optional respects their level of knowledge while still supporting developers who need the implementation detail.

items.title: Specialist workspace navigation with session context transfer
items.description: As a GoA developer, I need to navigate directly from a planning session to a specialist workspace for any recommended ADSP service. The specialist workspace shall launch with the relevant session context pre-loaded. I shall be able to return to the planning session from the specialist workspace without losing my place in either context.
items.rationale: Developers need a seamless transition from the planning context to service-specific technical guidance without manually re-entering context. Pre-loaded session context ensures the specialist agent can provide immediately relevant answers rather than requiring the developer to re-explain the problem.

items.title: Pattern library management interface for tenant administrators
items.description: As an ADSP tenant administrator, I need an administrative interface to create, edit, deactivate, and view business pattern templates. The interface shall present a form with all required pattern fields, validate input before submission, and display confirmation before saving. The list view shall show pattern name, status, and last modified date with search and filter capability.
items.rationale: Tenant administrators need a self-service interface to customize the pattern library for their organization's domain without requiring developer intervention. Front-end validation and confirmation dialogs prevent accidental misconfiguration of shared resources that affect all users in the tenant.

items.title: Session export with accessible keyboard-operable download control
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need a clearly labelled Export button on the session detail view that downloads the session plan as a JSON file named using the session title and date. I shall receive a success confirmation after the download initiates. The export action shall be fully keyboard-accessible and announced correctly to screen readers.
items.rationale: Session export allows analysts to share planning outputs with stakeholders who do not have planner-service access, and provides a portable record for project documentation. Keyboard-accessible export controls ensure the feature is available to all users regardless of input device.

items.title: AI processing progress indicator with screen reader announcement
items.description: As a GoA business analyst, I need a visible progress indicator in the chat interface whenever the AI is processing my message. The indicator shall appear within 1 second of message submission and shall distinguish between waiting for the AI to start and the AI actively streaming a response. The indicator shall disappear when the response is complete and its state shall be announced to screen readers.
items.rationale: LLM processing times are variable and unpredictable. Without a progress indicator, users cannot distinguish between the system processing and the system being broken, which leads to redundant submissions and user frustration. Screen reader announcements ensure blind and low-vision users receive the same awareness of processing state.
